description: Stage one of driving sessions on another machine you can ssh into, with nothing installed there. The second slice adds the ssh transport and a probe that checks a host over ssh (tmux and its version, the login shell, the agents, whether the far box runs its own Carnivore) and stores what it found.
examples: Add the studio computer from the hosts page, probe it to check ssh, tmux and the agents it has, then pick it in the new-session dialog to launch a claude session there.
Script your machines through the API instead of the page: one POST per box; the hosts page reads and writes the same routes.
Pair the studio computer from the discovered list with one click, then revoke the grant you gave it when it is sold, or unpair to end both sides at once.
how_to: Open Pack (press h with the drawer menu focused, or go to /#hosts), open the computers tab, and press "add a computer" for a label and an ssh target (an alias from your ~/.ssh/config, or user@host); the port and tmux socket are optional. The server generates the host's key; it shows up in the detail pane once the host is added.

Open the new row and press "probe" to check it over ssh: tmux and its version, the login shell, the agents it has, and whether it runs its own Carnivore. A failed probe names why (unreachable, ssh authentication failed, host key not verified, tmux too old); fix it and probe again.
Its status is read off its own pane (a permission dialog there reads question), with host_state down and status unknown while its host is unreachable; after a restart it comes back on its row and id.

Restart it from its row menu (the picker previews its far pane), or restart a stopped one from the launchpad: it comes back on its host, on the same row, resuming its conversation, but only once the host is reachable and confirms the old session is gone.

Or drive it through the API directly: POST /api/v1/hosts to add, GET to list, PATCH to edit, DELETE to remove, POST /api/v1/hosts/{key}/probe to check it, and POST /sessions with host_key set to a probed host to launch there.

If its ssh host key is already trusted here nothing is typed and the pairing finishes; on first contact the dialog asks for a code, which you get by pressing "show a code" on the other computer's own hosts page and typing its pairing id and code here. A computer Bonjour cannot see (a tailnet, another network) is added with "pair a computer": its name or ssh target.

A paired computer shows one of: connected, connecting, disconnected (the link is down and retrying), incompatible (its carnivore speaks another protocol), unpaired (it dropped its grant) or identity changed (its key is not the pinned one: unpair and pair again). A computer that is both an ssh host and a paired computer sits under one heading.
name: Remote tmux hosts
summary: add the machines you can ssh into as hosts, and run sessions on them from here.
where: Pack page: the computers tab, over ssh filter (#pack/ssh, or the old /#hosts and /#settings/hosts fragments). With the drawer menu focused, press h.
The host picker in the new-session dialog, right after choosing a provider.
A remote session's host label on its drawer row, beside its status light.
The PAIRING tab's pair a computer, show a code, advertising, rescan and rotate key controls, and its found on this network group; a paired computer's detail pane on MACHINES.
